### pelotero.c1: Six jointed legs and low, wide carapace

Trait ← Stable footing required in tall grass and uneven litter ← Low center of gravity prevents lateral tumbling ← Dense air amplifies wind force per meter per second on exposed meadows ← F4, F19

- **Skill:** Wind-Anchor (Defence): It clings tightly to grass stems and remains firmly anchored during strong winds.
- **Weakness:** Stationary for 3 seconds, vulnerable to bite attacks
- **Observe:**
  1. Watch it lock its tarsi into grass blades when the breeze picks up.
  2. Count six legs; the middle pair acts as stabilizers rather than climbers.
  3. See its wide, flattened back catch the wind without rolling over.
- **Journal:** It doesn't fight the wind; it becomes part of the meadow.
- **Plausibility:** plausible (judge astrobio/foodweb-2026-11-21, 2026-11-21)
  - A 3.2 cm, 0.4 g hexapod in tall meadow grass matches island detritivore size and the empty small-invertebrate decomposer niche (D28, D30). A low, wide body lowers the center of gravity on uneven litter; tarsal gripping on stems is standard for plant-dwelling Coleoptera. F19’s 1.6× wind loading matters most in exposed swards and during frontal gales; grass canopy shelters much of the litter layer, but open-patch anchoring still pays off.
